key_insight: OmniVBench introduces a new benchmark and large-scale dataset designed for the next generation of reference-to-video generation, where models must handle many reference types and combinations, not just one simple reference. It shifts evaluation from overall similarity to whether the model truly preserves, separates, and uses different reference factors correctly.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of comprehensive benchmarks for omni reference-to-video generation. Existing evaluations cover too few reference scenarios and often miss whether models can disentangle and route multiple reference factors instead of only matching them holistically.
method: Builds a benchmark covering diverse reference types and compositions for omni R2V generation.
Creates a large-scale dataset to support broader and more realistic evaluation settings.
Proposes evaluation protocols that test preservation, disentanglement, and routing of reference factors rather than only global consistency.
impact: This benchmark gives researchers a more realistic way to measure progress in video generation systems that use references. For practitioners, it helps identify whether a model is genuinely controllable and robust in complex, multi-reference scenarios.

paper_title: OmniVBench: A Benchmark and Large-Scale Dataset for Omni Reference-to-Video Generation
paper_authors: Wenxue Li, Peiyan Guan, Haoyang Jiang, Junxian Cai, Hualuo Liu
